results.correct_value: Snow usually lingers on the upper mountain in early July and thins to patches over loose ash and boulders by late July
results.evidence: The Mount St. Helens Institute notes Climbers Bivouac has opened in early-to-mid July in recent years because of snow. An Oregon Hikers thread reports continuous snow from about 7,000 ft to the summit on July 2, and a July 2021 trip report still found snow patches on the upper route. July is therefore not 'typically snow-free'; the month row was the outlier against optimalWindow and best_season.

results.correct_value: Coverage is limited to none; at best spotty, intermittent signal higher on the ridge depending on carrier
results.evidence: The Mount St. Helens Institute states there is limited to no cell service on the access roads or the climbing route itself. An Oregon Hikers climb report calls reception spotty, and a 2024 trip report (AT&T) found none through the forest and only intermittent bars higher up. No source supports 'intermittent-to-good'; watch_out and emergency already agree with the sources, so only comms is softened.

results.fact: Avalanche hazard in the route's season
results.correct_value: June: Low (not N/A) — lingering snow on the upper slopes can still slide in late spring/early summer
results.evidence: The Mount St. Helens Institute states avalanches can and do occur in winter, spring and early summer, and advises avalanche training and tools whenever snow is on the ground. The Forest Service says the mountain has big avalanches October through May (silent on June). Internally, approach, approach_variants[0].hazards[4], pitch_detail[2] and the June month row all treat June as a snow climb with avalanche awareness; only the avalanche panel says N/A. June set to Low, matching May, and the zone text qualified.
